output.summary: An evergreen oak native to the western Mediterranean, with most of its population in the Iberian Peninsula and smaller populations in Northwest Africa. It has a dense, rounded crown and small, leathery leaves. Humans have eaten its acorns since Neolithic times, including toasted and ground as flour for soups or breads in southern Iberia.
output.edibilityNote: Acorns are eaten; in Neolithic southern Iberia they were gently toasted, ground into flour, and used in soups or breads.
